Dorchester Historical Society
195 Boston Street Dorchester, Massachusetts 02125
September 24, 1975
Ms. Lynda Laird Weisberg
Research Planning Associates, Inc.
Lh Brattle Street
Cambridge, Massachusetts 02138
Dear Ms. Weisberg:
In regard to your letter and enclosures of Sept.22,1975, we understand the enclosures to be a listing of buildings being considered for demolition by the City of Boston. After reviewing this list in the light of Public Law 89-665 (as ammended), Executive Order 11593 and the various guidelines set forth by the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, we find that we have no positive knowledge that a negative impact would result from any demolition. There certainly would be no direct or indirect impact on any property currently listed, pending listing, or under active consideration for listing on the National Register of Historic Places by the National Register or the State Historic Preservation Office and its Review Board (in this case the Massachusetts Historical Commission).
However there exists no suitable inventory of the area that would allow us to determine if any of the properties scheduled for demolition or properties that might be adversly affected by their demolition would meet the requirements for listing on the National Register. Indeed given the large number of properties under consideration it seems probable that at least some (albeit very few ) would meet these requirements either as individual properties or parts of districts. This is especially true since many of the demolitions will occur in areas known to contain properties of historical, social, cultural and architectural significance.
Particularly sensitive areas include; the east side of Washington Street centering on Mellville Avenue, the area known as Jone's Hill centering on Cushing Avenue and the area known as Harrison Equare centering on Mill Street.
It seems that given the diversity of the area you are faced with the rather impossible task of proving a negative. In any event in the absence of at least a preliminary on site inspection of each property little can be said with certainty.
Cont.
